goal: Review and lock the complete product contract for switchable, semantically equivalent layout profiles.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Requirements.md` and the client-facing layout terminology in `PRODUCT.md`, `docs/functionality/CLIENT-DESKTOP.md`, `apps/desktop/README.md`, and `apps/desktop/Design.md`. Context: the current code exposes two partial desktop shell strings while the requested product behavior covers complete desktop and mobile presentation systems. Target: confirm REQ-001 through REQ-014, users, workflows, scope, non-goals, and final acceptance without redefining feature capability or server policy. Design Considerations: keep profile identity semantic, separate user selection from responsive variants, and define capability parity across layouts. Design Value: a fixed product contract prevents renderer work from silently weakening state continuity or calling a shell-only change complete. Constraints & Risks: preserve the current client product boundary, do not add remote layout code, and update requirements before implementation if evidence changes the target.

acceptance_criteria.text: Requirements.md defines the user problem, desktop/mobile workflows, scope, non-goals, fourteen stable requirement labels, and one final acceptance target.
The contract requires whole-presentation profiles and explicitly preserves layout-neutral product capabilities, authorization, and active task state.
The contract defines workbench and studio as semantic current identities and contains no numbered, versioned, legacy, or compatibility plan structure.

goal: Revalidate repository gaps and primary framework practices behind the layout design.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Evidence.md` plus current shell, appearance, controller, preference, settings, tests, architecture verifier, product docs, and official Flutter/first-party workbench references. Context: direct IDs, uncoordinated writes, asynchronous hydration, feature-level branches, a fixed mobile shell, and contradictory design text are observable in the working tree. Target: keep every major requirement and architecture choice tied to a file, symbol, test gap, user fact, or primary/open-source practice. Design Considerations: distinguish evidence from inference; compare adaptive resolution, state identity, restoration, theme extension, registry, and reset practices. Design Value: evidence prevents a generic plugin-style abstraction and justifies only the patterns that remove observed coupling or races. Constraints & Risks: cite relative repository paths and public sources only; do not record local identity, raw runtime data, conversations, devices, or secrets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Evidence.md traces the current selection, rendering, persistence, theme, mobile, test, and verifier paths with observed gaps.
Primary Flutter sources support adaptive constraint resolution, state ownership/restoration, ThemeExtension composition, and bounded widget work.

Contradictory documentation, the missing coverage command, dirty-worktree constraint, and seven pre-existing sibling-plan validation issues are recorded without being reclassified as layout deliverables.

goal: Finalize the requirement-to-evidence matrix before layout code changes begin.
description: Scope: `docs/plan/layout-management/Validation.md`, planned layout contract/manager/store/widget tests, architecture checks, Better Plan checks, and existing client commands. Context: current tests prove static shell shapes but not live switching, atomicity, recovery, state continuity, full destination coverage, visual difference, or mobile behavior. Target: map every LAY requirement to deterministic foundation evidence and named desktop/mobile child evidence. Design Considerations: separate unit, widget, golden, integration, build, launch, and authorized-device claims; establish a real coverage command before using coverage as evidence. Design Value: agreeing on proof before implementation prevents easy structural tests from replacing product behavior. Constraints & Risks: aggregate `client:verify` has runtime-data side effects and requires later explicit authorization; store/channel publication is not layout validation.

acceptance_criteria.text: Validation.md maps all fourteen requirements to concrete foundation and child-plan evidence.
The matrix covers registry, transaction, corruption, concurrency, destination parity, adaptive resize, state/focus continuity, accessibility, goldens, integration, architecture, build, and launch.
Every listed current command exists; any planned coverage or layout-integration command is explicitly identified as work to establish rather than existing evidence.

goal: Lock the module map, contracts, state machine, data structures, patterns, and child-plan boundaries.
description: Scope: docs/plan/layout-management/Architecture.md and initial interfaces under contracts/presentation, application/features/layout, platform/presentation, and frontend/layout. Context: one string branch cannot scale to isolated full presentation systems, while the plan audit found a desktop/mobile medium-key collision, duplicate catalog/registry ownership, and a parent/child validation cycle. Target: establish inward dependencies, one responsibility per module, explicit runtime surface and viewport dimensions, immutable bundle manifests, one parent-integration-owned composition root, preview/commit state machine, typed preference repository, semantic destination coverage, ThemeExtension composition, bounded restoration, and disjoint desktop/mobile child ownership. Design Considerations: immutable O(1) maps, O(P×S×V×D) composition validation, one active resolution cache, serialized writes, one active widget tree, fixture-only foundation validation, and complete-removal rules. Design Value: the selected patterns remove branch leakage, key collisions, duplicate registration, stale writes, hidden routes, theme duplication, cross-profile coupling, and state loss. Constraints & Risks: foundation core must not import built-in renderer bundles; profiles may not import each other, ClientController, legacy shell, backend/platform, or shared styled components; no service locator, codegen layer, remote code, versioned directory, or compatibility path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Architecture.md records the module/file map, responsibility boundaries, dependency direction, interface contracts, state machine, algorithms, and complexity.
Registry/Factory, Strategy, State Machine/Command, Repository, and ThemeExtension choices are justified against simpler alternatives; deliberately simple areas stay pattern-free.
Desktop and mobile child plans own disjoint variant modules and their architecture criteria verify the parent contract before implementation.
Initial scaffold compiles without moving business logic into frontend profile modules.

Architecture.md defines LayoutRuntimeSurface and LayoutVariantKey(profile, surface, viewport), fixture-only foundation validation, profile-owned surface bundles, and one parent-integration-owned composition root with O(P×S×V×D) exact coverage validation.
Architecture fixes the required surface policy to desktop medium/expanded and mobile compact/medium, with no unsupported key or cross-surface fallback.

goal: Implement pure presentation contracts and one canonical semantic destination catalog.
description: Scope: apps/desktop/lib/src/contracts/presentation/*.dart, application/features/navigation/semantic_destination_catalog.dart, localized metadata keys, and focused tests. Context: destination lists and aliases are distributed across models, shell navigation, search, README text, and source-string verifiers; desktop and mobile also share the name medium but require different renderer variants. Target: immutable profile, runtime-surface, viewport, composite variant key, selection, preferences, and destination values plus one exact current destination authority consumed through declared interfaces. Design Considerations: profile identity stays semantic; LayoutRuntimeSurface is explicit but not persisted; aliases resolve before layout composition; deterministic sets/maps support tests; contracts import no implementation layer. Design Value: one semantic catalog and collision-free composite key let every layout prove equivalent reachability without duplicating navigation policy. Constraints & Risks: preserve current section behavior and capability filtering; do not add feature availability or server policy to presentation descriptors.

acceptance_criteria.text: Contract tests prove immutable parsing/validation, semantic names, deterministic equality/order, viewport classification inputs, and safe error codes.
The destination catalog exactly represents current reachable client surfaces and aliases without importing frontend/platform/backend implementations.

evidence_refs.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; fs=list(Path('apps/desktop/lib/src/contracts/presentation').glob('*.dart'))+[Path('apps/desktop/lib/src/application/features/navigation/semantic_destination_catalog.dart')]; forbidden=('src/frontend/','src/platform/','src/backend/'); assert not [(str(f),x) for f in fs for x in forbidden if x in f.read_text()]"

acceptance_criteria.text: No duplicate shell module list is introduced in the new layout modules.

evidence_refs.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; roots=[Path('apps/desktop/lib/src/application/features/layout'),Path('apps/desktop/lib/src/frontend/layout')]; fs=[f for r in roots if r.exists() for f in r.rglob('*.dart')]; assert not [str(f) for f in fs if 'ClientSection.' in f.read_text()]"

acceptance_criteria.text: Contract tests prove desktop/medium and mobile/medium produce distinct LayoutVariantKey values while persisting only the shared semantic profile ID.
Environment contract tests prove surface-bounded viewport classification: narrow desktop remains desktop/medium and large mobile remains mobile/medium.

commit.message: feat(client): add layout and destination contracts

goal: Implement the immutable profile catalog, exact-set validator, adaptive resolver, and bounded presentation-state store.
description: Scope: application/features/layout/layout_catalog.dart, layout_resolver.dart, layout_state_store.dart, and focused unit tests. Context: ShellLayoutIds.all is linear and carries no coverage/default/surface/viewport/state-boundary contract; a profile-plus-viewport key would collide for desktop/medium and mobile/medium. Target: immutable maps keyed by profile and LayoutVariantKey(profile,surface,viewport), cached ordered metadata, deterministic exact-product validation, O(1) active resolution, and bounded presentation-only state keyed by registered profile/surface/destination/surface. Design Considerations: validate once per catalog revision in O(P×S×V×D); cache only the active tuple; fail registration rather than falling back across profiles or surfaces for missing destinations. Design Value: composite map lookup and exact-set validation prevent key collisions, branch scans, and incomplete layouts while keeping runtime cost constant. Constraints & Risks: no unbounded LRU is needed because valid keys are catalog-bounded; state values cannot contain business data, conversation content, paths, or secrets.

acceptance_criteria.text: Catalog tests reject duplicate IDs, missing/duplicate defaults, numbered identities, incomplete viewport or destination coverage, and mismatched revisions.
Resolver tests prove stable selected identity across resize, deterministic default recovery, and O(1) map-based active lookup without catalog scans in build paths.
Presentation-state tests prove valid-key bounds, per-profile isolation, deterministic reset, and rejection of unregistered keys.
Catalog tests prove the complete profile × surface × viewport × destination product and reject desktop/mobile medium-key collisions, missing surfaces, and extra surface coverage.
Catalog and resolver tests prove the exact desktop medium/expanded and mobile compact/medium products with no unsupported viewport or cross-surface fallback.

commit.message: feat(client): add deterministic layout catalog and resolver

goal: Implement transactional presentation preferences and the preview/commit layout manager.
description: Scope: `contracts/presentation/presentation_preferences.dart`, `platform/presentation/presentation_preferences_repository.dart`, `application/features/layout/layout_manager.dart`, controller composition, startup hydration, and tests. Context: three uncoordinated read-modify-write setters can lose fields; layout UI is notified before persistence succeeds; non-default startup can flash the default shell. Target: one typed canonical preference document, serialized atomic commits, loading/stable/previewing/committing/error states, monotonic operation epochs, confirm/cancel/reset, deterministic default recovery, and first-shell hydration. Design Considerations: preview is memory-only; confirm persists before promotion; stale completions cannot win; safe errors are bounded codes; appearance catalog loading remains separate. Design Value: the transaction converts a race-prone mutable string into an auditable user action with rollback. Constraints & Risks: ignore and remove the retired `shellLayoutId` field rather than dual-reading it; preserve appearance and locale values; do not log raw documents or local paths.

acceptance_criteria.text: Repository tests prove serialized concurrent layout/appearance/locale updates, atomic replacement, canonical output, corrupt-file recovery, and no retired field on write.
Manager tests prove initialize, preview, confirm, cancel, reset, timeout, invalid/unavailable ID, save failure rollback, and stale-operation suppression.
The first meaningful shell waits for preference hydration and failures expose only a localized safe error state.
ClientController no longer owns a second mutable layout string or independent layout preference setter.

goal: Implement profile-agnostic frontend host interfaces and fixture validation without importing built-in renderers.
description: Scope: apps/desktop/lib/src/frontend/layout/layout_surface_bundle.dart, layout_definition.dart, layout_registry.dart, layout_host.dart, layout_scope.dart, layout_visual_tokens.dart, layout_component_kit.dart, layout_focus_coordinator.dart, fixture-only tests, apps/desktop/scripts/verify-layout-boundaries.mjs, and its package command. Context: renderer children require stable host interfaces before they can build disjoint bundles, but real workbench/studio registration and app cutover must wait for both children. Target: deliver independently testable frontend contracts, immutable fixture registry/host behavior, ThemeExtension composition, semantic focus restoration, and enforceable import/ownership rules with no built-in profile dependency. Design Considerations: builders stay frontend-only; component kit defines roles rather than shared styled widgets; LayoutHost builds one active fixture tree; profile path manifests and forbidden imports are statically checked. Design Value: this node breaks the parent/child cycle and gives parallel profile work a stable boundary without pre-registering unfinished layouts. Constraints & Risks: do not edit app.dart, ClientShell, Settings, a built-in profile directory, or the final composition root; do not keep inactive fixture trees mounted.

acceptance_criteria.text: LayoutSurfaceBundle, LayoutDefinition, LayoutRegistry, LayoutHost, LayoutScope, LayoutVisualTokens, LayoutComponentKit, and LayoutFocusCoordinator compile without importing built-in profiles, ClientController, legacy shell, backend, or platform implementations.
Fixture tests prove exact profile/surface/viewport/destination parity, one active tree, deterministic token composition, semantic focus fallback, bounded restoration namespaces, and scoped rebuilds.

npm run client:verify:layouts runs a self-tested owned-path and import verifier that rejects cross-profile dependencies, complete-controller imports, legacy shell imports, backend/platform imports, shared styled components, mutable registration, and unauthorized composition-root imports.
Desktop and mobile architecture documents can name these exact current interfaces while retaining disjoint renderer-owned paths.

goal: Compose the four verified surface bundles, cut the app over to the single layout host, and remove every superseded renderer path.
description: Scope: frontend/layout/built_in_layout_composition.dart, the immutable production registry, lib/app.dart, ClientController composition, ClientShell entry, desktop/mobile Settings selector, theme composition, focus/state integration, architecture verifier, localization, product/design docs, and complete retired-path removal. Context: foundation core and the desktop/mobile child plans supply four isolated LayoutSurfaceBundle entry points; no renderer child may edit shared integration files. Target: import each bundle exactly once, derive pure catalog/widget registry/Settings metadata from that one composition, make LayoutHost the only desktop and mobile renderer, expose preview/confirm/cancel/reset/error UX, and delete old shell IDs, stores, branches, widgets, tests, and contradictory docs. Design Considerations: composition validation is O(P×S×V×D) once; only active profile mounts; layout/appearance axes compose; cold start waits for preferences; cross-plan receipts are checked before this Node starts. Design Value: one join point preserves independent profile ownership while guaranteeing whole-product coverage and an atomic migration. Constraints & Risks: do not edit profile internals or duplicate bundle metadata; start only after both renderer child plans have proven their workbench and studio surface bundles; preserve unrelated working-tree changes and privacy boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.text: Frontend registry tests prove exact ID parity with the pure catalog, exact destination/viewport builders, one default, and deterministic previews.
Theme tests compose every built-in appearance palette with both layout token families without resetting the appearance selection.
Focus/restoration tests prove semantic restoration without a whole-tree GlobalKey or permanently mounted inactive profiles.
Architecture verification forbids profile-ID checks outside registration/tests and validates destination coverage through structure rather than source-string placement.
Desktop and mobile child receipts prove all four required LayoutSurfaceBundle entry points, their profile-owned tests/goldens, and disjoint owned-path manifests before production composition begins.
Built-in composition imports each bundle exactly once and derives the pure catalog, widget registry, and ordered Settings metadata without a second manual profile list.
LayoutHost is the only desktop/mobile renderer and Settings supports semantic preview, confirm, cancel, reset, loading, committing, localized error, keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion behavior.

ShellLayoutIds, shellLayoutId, old preference methods/key, direct profile branches, old desktop/mobile shell builders, fixed bottom navigation, numbered labels/tests, and contradictory documentation are removed with no compatibility path.

goal: Prove the complete layout plan family, rebuild and open the desktop client, and independently verify the Android build.
description: Scope: foundation, desktop, and mobile requirement matrices; all layout unit/widget/golden/integration/architecture gates; scoped Better Plan checks; canonical macOS rebuild/open; independent Android debug build and authorized device handling. Context: this Node follows the parent integration join and is the only family-wide acceptance claim; renderer child tests alone cannot prove the wired app. Target: prove every foundation and child requirement, both materially different profiles on desktop/mobile surfaces, state-safe switching, hard isolation, complete migration, and real client build/launch behavior. Design Considerations: command/file-backed evidence stays privacy-minimal; desktop launch, Android build, simulator/device, packaging, release, security, and stores remain separate claims. Design Value: one final family receipt prevents narrow profile tests from being misreported as a complete client. Constraints & Risks: run the Android build through an independent verification subagent and install/launch only when an authorized device is connected; full-workspace Better Plan closure still requires unrelated release-plan graph debt to be repaired separately.

acceptance_criteria.text: All foundation unit/widget/architecture checks mapped in Validation.md pass with command or file evidence.
Static evidence proves ShellLayoutIds, shellLayoutId, old preference read/write methods, numbered layout labels, and direct profile branches are absent from current implementation paths.
npm run client:format:check, client:analyze, client:test, client:verify:architecture, client:verify:plan, and client:contracts:test pass.
Scoped Better Plan validate --check-sources and check-labels pass for layout-management, and desktop/mobile child architecture criteria resolve against the same current contract files.
Desktop and mobile child final-validation Nodes are completed with profile-owned command/file evidence and scoped label/manifest checks.
npm run client:run:macos rebuilds and opens the current client; both profiles and representative destinations are inspected without exposing runtime data.

An independent verification subagent runs npm run client:build:android:debug and reports build, discovery, authorization, install, and launch statuses separately when an authorized phone is available.
Scoped validate --check-sources and check-labels pass for the foundation, desktop, and mobile plans; any unrelated full-workspace plan debt is reported without weakening layout evidence.
